title: Leftover-word cells at a Juggler near-convergent apply to a one-parameter Christoffel necklace
statement: At a leftover near-convergent length L with o = o_min(L), leftover-itinerary cells or CycleMin-legal expanding itineraries of weight o concentrate on the Christoffel / mechanical necklace of slope o/L (cyclic Hamming radius O(1) or o(L)), so those cells apply to a one-parameter family instead of C(L, o) words.
counterexamples: L=11: thirty first-expanding short-gap leftovers have cyclic Hamming histogram 0:1, 2:16, 4:13 versus necklace size 4; OOOOOOOEEEE is distance 4
L=19: 12376 CycleMin weight-12 words, median cyclic Hamming 6, radius 0 only 7, radius ≤ 2 only 389
L=19 isolated-even worst-m family has 462 words, not 7; finance and CycleMin slack 139 are word-order-independent
notes: Fernández–Ibáñez maximizers need the Collatz affine / Terras constant C, which Juggler does not have. Lebel modular sieving is not transferred. Cycle-only near-Christoffel rigidity (a realized cycle itinerary must be close to the necklace) is not refuted and is the same open question as cycle-only near-tightness. Not a leftover-length exclusion and not a halt theorem.
tested_range: leftover records 38,84,569,1054 plus killed near-convergents 11,19; thirty L=11 leftovers; all CycleMin weight-o_min words at L=11,19
